Chronic Heart Failure Management

Corvanta: A New Approach to Chronic Heart Failure

Understanding the core patient profile can aid in effective disease management and treatment planning.

Presenter / Audience: Healthcare Professionals

Core Patient Profile

Adults with chronic heart failure
Patient Population
Requiring ongoing pharmacologic management.
Stable or recently stabilized
Disease Status
Outpatient population.
Persistent dyspnea, fatigue
Symptom Burden
Exercise intolerance, or fluid-retention risk.

Key Message

Key Message

Risk stratification is essential for optimizing treatment outcomes in patients with chronic heart failure.

Prior Treatment and Care Setting

The prior treatment for the core patient profile includes background heart-failure therapy already initiated or being optimized.

  • Cardiology clinic
  • Internal medicine clinic
  • Heart-failure program
  • Transitional-care pathway

Eligibility Criteria

1

Chronic Heart Failure Diagnosis Duration

At least 6 months.

2

NYHA Functional Class

II to III at baseline.

3

Background Care Stability Duration

At least 4 weeks.

4

Safety Considerations

Renal function monitoring is critical in the management of chronic heart failure.

Important Safety Information (ISI)

Cardionex: Important Safety Information

Corvanta is the brand name for Cardionex, a simulated investigational therapeutic concept for chronic heart failure management in adults. The intended role is adjunctive support alongside optimized standard heart-failure care.

  • Risk: Hypersensitivity reactions.
  • Trigger / Setting: Initiation in patients with known hypersensitivity.
  • Action for HCP: Discontinue if hypersensitivity occurs.
  • Monitoring: Monitor for worsening heart failure symptoms.
  • Contraindications: Known history of serious hypersensitivity to Cardionex.
